title: Soft failsafe allocator and graceful burst degradation plan
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Summary: A weekend capacity incident in a Dedicated cluster exposed brittle reservation sizing and an uncompromising burst policy. Multiple tenants experienced evictions when one tenant produced heavy, short-duration spikes; cascading scheduler pressure resulted in tail latency and customer-visible failures. This ticket defines a combined mitigation roadmap: a soft failsafe allocation layer, controlled burst degradation paths, and stronger telemetry/alarms so we can avoid large-scale evictions while preserving throughput for healthy tenants.

Scope: changes to the cluster allocator, tenant-level soft caps and decay-based burst tokens, scheduler eviction attenuation (hysteresis), autoscaler guardrails for reservation adjustments, and new observability panels and SLO checks. Focused on Dedicated clusters for the 2026-Q2 cadence but designs should be compatible with Private deployments.

Root causes identified: 1) Reservation sizing mismatch: several tenants had long-running reservations with low utilization but their allocation prevented the scheduler from reclaiming capacity quickly. 2) Burst token model: a single tenant could exhaust device-local tokens triggering large preemption waves. 3) Eviction policy thresholding is binary (no hysteresis) causing oscillation. 4) Limited telemetry: we lacked a concise signal combining instantaneous GPU pressure, queue latency, and token-source attribution to trigger mitigations early.
action_items: Design and implement a soft failsafe allocator layer that can mark a subset of reservation capacity as reclaimable under sustained pressure (soft_cap with TTL and decay).
Introduce per-tenant burst budget decay model (leaky-bucket) with configurable degradation curve instead of instantaneous hard exhaust.
Add eviction hysteresis: require pressure to persist for N seconds and scale eviction aggressiveness gradually to avoid wholesale preemption.
Implement a reservation autoscaler validator that flags and suggests right-sizing recommendations when utilization & request pattern mismatch is detected.
Create new composite telemetry signal 'cluster_pressure_index' combining GPU utilization, queued-request-count, and recent eviction-rate; wire alerts at two thresholds (warning/critical).
Add a read-only tenant sandbox mode to simulate burst behavior without impacting production neighbors for testing.
Update runbooks: include step-by-step mitigation steps using soft-cap toggles, burst-reduction, and reservation shrink procedures.
Ship a canary in one Dedicated cluster with feature-flagged rollout and automated rollback if tail-latency or error-rate regressions exceed guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Cluster in canary sees no >50% spike in eviction rate when subjected to controlled tenant spike tests that previously caused evictions.
Tail P99 latency for neighboring tenants degrades by <15% under identical spike workload during canary.
Autoscaler generates right-sizing proposals with accuracy >75% against historical usage for a 14-day lookback in tests.
New 'cluster_pressure_index' alerts fire before eviction wave in synthetic load tests and provide attribution to tenant or subsystem.
Feature flags allow immediate rollback without requiring infra migration and have matched docs for on-call.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): Implement allocator hooks and run unit and integration tests in staging. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable feature flag in a single low-traffic Dedicated cluster for 48h with synthetic spike tests and manual verification. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand canary to 3 clusters across regions with automated SLO checks gating each expansion window. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (global): Default-on for new reservations; existing reservations can opt-in or be suggested via autoscaler. Monitor for 2 weeks then flip for all clusters. Duration: 1 week.
Rollback: Feature-flag-based immediate disable; if rollback occurs, run deep postmortem and revert autoscaler recommendations.
testing_plan: Synthetic spike harness: reproduce the prior incident pattern (1 tenant heavy 3–10s bursts every 30s) and measure eviction and P99 impact before/after.
Chaos tests: simulate delayed heartbeats and node reboots to ensure soft-cap state converges and does not leak.
Load tests: run long-running low-utilization reservations concurrent with bursty tenants to validate reclaimability.
On-call dry-run: have SREs walk through runbook steps during canary and confirm operator-visible knobs work as expected.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metric: cluster_pressure_index (0-100) derived from GPU_util*0.5 + queued_requests_norm*0.3 + eviction_rate_norm*0.2.
Alert: cluster_pressure_index > 60 for 30s -> page on-call SRE (warning).
Alert: cluster_pressure_index > 85 for 15s -> auto-engage mitigation playbook, notify PMEs and account owners (critical).
Dashboards: per-tenant burst_budget, soft_cap_usage, eviction_trigger_trace (recent N events), reservation_utilization_heatmap.
Add logs: include allocation decision reasons and token attribution (which tenant consumed tokens from which pool) with sampling for high cardinality.
